Yes. 

Even though the story is very short, both characters (one physically present, one present only in memory) are given an appropriate and compelling level of complexity. Clara is established as a round, observant character whose emotional depth is revealed through her sensory interactions with her childhood home and the dissonance between her memories and reality. Meanwhile, her absent mother is quickly elevated from a potentially flat background figure into a complex character through a single, chilling detail: the memory of the soap used to scrub away "garden soil—and once, something completely different." This hint of a dark, shared backstory ensures neither character feels one-dimensional or merely like a plot device.
